analysis.investment_thesis: Network18 is a capital-destroying media conglomerate with a 0.76% ROE, persistently negative free cash flow, and a P/E of 153x on near-zero earnings — the antithesis of a wonderful business. The ongoing Reliance-driven restructuring has produced wildly erratic financials, making intrinsic value nearly impossible to calculate.
key_strengths: Recognizable media brands (CNBC-TV18, MoneyControl, News18) with real audience reach in business and news segments
Reliance Industries parentage (56.89% promoter stake) provides implicit financial backstop and distribution muscle
P/B of 1.11x suggests limited further downside on a pure asset basis
key_risks: Chronically cash-destructive: operating CF negative in 4 of last 5 years, FCF was -8,869 Cr in FY24 and -2,809 Cr in FY25
Earnings are illusory — 'Other Income' swung from +801 Cr (FY24) to -734 Cr (FY25) to +449 Cr (FY26), masking operational rot; operating margin is -4.36%
Radical restructuring (total assets collapsed from 39,881 Cr in FY24 to 8,498 Cr in FY25) makes business continuity and true earnings power unknowable
red_flags: ROE of 0.76% — a company that earns nothing on equity is not a business, it's a liability
P/E of 153x on FY26 earnings of ~155 Cr that appear entirely driven by one-time Other Income (449 Cr), not operations
Revenue collapsed 77% from 9,297 Cr (FY24) to 2,121 Cr (FY26) — restructuring or not, this level of discontinuity disqualifies predictable earnings power
Net loss of 1,777 Cr in FY25 wiped out years of accumulated reserves
Minority shareholders are effectively passengers in a Reliance corporate reorganisation they did not vote for
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I spent decades looking for businesses I can understand, with durable competitive advantages, run by honest managers, priced at fair values. Network18 fails on nearly every count. The ROE is 0.76% — I won't touch a business that earns less than a savings account on shareholder equity. The operating margin is negative (-4.36%), and free cash flow has been negative in four of the last five years, totalling roughly -13,300 Cr of cash burned. Finance costs have compounded at 11% annually (80 Cr in FY17 to 477 Cr in FY25), meaning the company is paying more and more just to stay afloat. A P/E of 153x for this kind of business is not a valuation — it is a speculation tax.

The restructuring story here is deeply opaque. Total assets ballooned to 39,881 Cr in FY24 (with CWIP alone at 11,627 Cr, likely Viacom18/JioCinema related), then shrank back to ~9,000 Cr in FY26. Revenue swung from 9,297 Cr to 2,121 Cr. Net profit went from -1,777 Cr in FY25 to +155 Cr in FY26, but that 155 Cr profit is entirely a mirage — Other Income alone was 449 Cr while operating income was just 44 Cr. I have a simple rule: if I cannot understand how a business earns its money, I do not own it. Network18 today is an accounting puzzle dressed up as a media company. At any price, this is not a business I would want to own.
